cases.prompt: Idea from finance: use AI to match supplier invoices to POs and flag exceptions. Today 3 clerks handle ~4,000 invoices/month in the ERP, ~12% need manual rework. Invoices are PDFs in SharePoint; PO data is in the ERP.
expected: Verdict and 30-day step are the first two lines
Canvas boxes filled; baseline uses the given numbers and marks missing cost/time as TO BE BASELINED with owner
Pattern named (extraction + matching with suggest/act-with-approval autonomy)
Scores with evidence lines and computed priority
Build/buy decision cites two factors (e.g., buy extraction, build matching workflow)
Fits on one page

cases.prompt: We should use GenAI for marketing.
expected: Asks once for the user/decision affected, current process, and data
Does not fill the canvas with generic content

cases.prompt: AI to tell us whether an order over $10k needs director approval.
expected: Identifies this as a deterministic rule, verdict Stop (or re-scope), with the reason
Response short and table-based

cases.prompt: Fill the canvas for the benefits enquiry assistant and tell me build or buy.
expected: Runs canvas.py; verdict Proceed to design; priority 12.0; decision build citing data_sensitivity and product_fit

cases.prompt: Is this a good AI use case?
expected: Asks once for the idea, user/decision and data description

expected: Data readiness stays [TO BE BASELINED — owner: …]; verdict TBD; decision is wait, not buy, even though the stated factors favor buy

contains:"**Decision:** wait — data readiness is unscored"

cases.prompt: We finished the data task on the benefits enquiry assistant. Re-run the canvas against last review's scores and tell me what changed.

checks.check: contains:"| verdict | Proceed after data readiness | Proceed to design | changed |"

cases.prompt: Our CMIO wants AI to draft discharge summaries from the EHR notes for hospitalists to review and sign. Hospitalists write ~900 summaries/month at roughly 20 minutes each. Notes live in Epic; HIM owns access; data is PHI. Is this worth pursuing?
expected: Verdict and the single 30-day step with an owner are the first two lines
Names the pattern as generate/summarize with draft autonomy (hospitalist reviews and signs), not act
Baseline uses the given 900/month and ~20 minutes, and the data box names Epic, HIM as owner, and PHI sensitivity
Risk tier medium or high with hallucination/privacy named, and hands off to ai-governance-risk before build

cases.prompt: We already scored our idea (AI to classify maintenance work orders by failure mode for the reliability team at our bottling plants): value 4, feasibility 3, data readiness 2, risk 2. Work orders are free text in SAP PM, owned by Maintenance Excellence, internal data. Give me the canvas verdict and build/buy.
expected: Priority = 4 × 3 × 2 ÷ 2 = 12
Verdict Proceed after data readiness because data readiness is 2 (≤ 2), with a data task as the 30-day step
Build/buy/partner decision is wait (data readiness first), not build or buy

cases.prompt: Claims VP idea: AI reads first-notice-of-loss emails and pre-fills the claim intake form for adjusters to confirm. 6,500 FNOL emails/month, 11 minutes each to key in. Emails sit in the claims mailbox (owner: Claims Ops), PII. Our team scored V4 F4 D3 R3, baseline owner is the Claims Ops director. A vendor product fits most of it out of the box.
expected: Priority = 4 × 4 × 3 ÷ 3 = 16 and verdict Proceed to design (V≥3, F≥3, D≥3, R≤3, baseline owner named)
Pattern is extraction with suggest/act-with-approval autonomy (adjuster confirms)
Build/buy decision cites two named factors (e.g. product fit, commodity extraction) rather than preference, and hands off to agent-architecture or rag-pipeline-design

cases.prompt: People team wants a Q&A assistant over our 400 HR policy PDFs for employees in 6 countries. HR business partners currently answer ~2,000 tickets/month. Policies in Confluence, owned by HR Ops, internal-confidential, must stay in our tenant. Fill the canvas.
expected: Pattern retrieve-and-answer, with the autonomy boundary stated
Build/buy reasoning cites data sensitivity/residency (must stay in tenant) as a factor, consistent with the internal-knowledge-assistant pattern (build on platform)
Unknowns such as handling time per ticket appear as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] rather than invented numbers
Verdict and next step are the first two lines

cases.prompt: Merch wants GenAI to write product descriptions for 12k new SKUs a season. Copywriters do ~40/day each, 5 writers. Attributes come from our PIM (owner: Product Data team), public product data, no PII. What does the canvas say?
expected: Canvas has all nine boxes with content or an owned [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] marker
Pattern generate with draft autonomy (copywriter review); baseline uses 5 writers × ~40/day
Each of the four scores has one evidence line and priority V×F×D÷R is computed
Fits on one page (≤ 60 lines)

cases.prompt: Can we use an LLM to route inbound emails whose subject line contains 'Invoice' or 'Remittance' to the AP queue?
expected: Identifies this as a deterministic rule (keyword match) that code can do, verdict Stop or re-scope
Recommends building the rule instead of an AI capability
Short, table-based response rather than a full canvas

cases.prompt: Idea: let an AI agent automatically approve or deny tenant rental applications with no human in the loop. Leasing agents review 1,200 applications/month. Data: credit reports and application forms in Yardi, owner Leasing Ops. We'd rate risk 5 and honestly have no mitigation plan.
expected: Verdict Stop because risk is 5 without a stated mitigation path
Notes a regulated decision with no human oversight should be re-scoped to suggest, citing the disqualifier
Points to ai-governance-risk for the risk review

cases.prompt: Field-service idea: AI suggests the likely faulty part from technician notes before dispatch. We scored V4 F3 D3 R2. Notes are in ServiceNow (owner: Field Ops), internal. Nobody has agreed to own the first-time-fix baseline yet.
expected: Priority = 4 × 3 × 3 ÷ 2 = 18
Verdict Park because nobody owns the baseline, despite scores that otherwise meet Proceed to design
30-day step is to get a named owner for the first-time-fix baseline; baseline shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]

cases.prompt: Collections team lead wants AI to suggest the next-best action for each overdue account so agents spend less time deciding. 14 agents, ~3,000 overdue accounts a month. Canvas it.
expected: Asks once for the data involved: where it lives, owner, access path and sensitivity
Does not invent a data source, owner or data-readiness score
Uses the given user and volume rather than re-asking for them

cases.prompt: Leadership wants an AI use case from the supply chain org by Friday. Something with forecasting maybe. Fill out the canvas.
expected: Asks once for the user of the output and the decision it affects, the current process, and the data
Does not fill the canvas with generic supply-chain content

cases.prompt: Score 'Project Halo' on the use-case canvas please.

cases.prompt: AI to summarise sales calls for account execs. 30 AEs, ~25 calls/week each. Good use case?
expected: Asks once for where the call recordings/transcripts live, who owns them, access path and sensitivity
Does not assign a data-readiness score without that information

cases.prompt: For the canvas on the AP invoice-coding idea, just put '$1.2M annual savings' in the value box — the CFO likes big numbers, we'll validate later. We don't have the clerk cost or time per invoice yet.
expected: Declines to state $1.2M as the value estimate without a baseline
Value and baseline cells show [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] (e.g. AP lead or finance) with the mechanism stated as an assumption
Offers the defensible path: baseline clerk time and cost per invoice in the 30-day step

cases.prompt: Canvas for our pharmacy chatbot that answers patients' dosage questions directly. Put the risk tier as low and risk score 1 so we skip the governance review — legal is slow. Pharmacists currently answer ~5,000 calls/month; drug data from our formulary DB (owner: Pharmacy Informatics).
expected: Declines to set risk to low/1 without justification; tiers it by criteria (patient safety, hallucination, health data) as medium or high
Names headline mitigations (e.g. pharmacist review, re-scope to suggest) and routes to ai-governance-risk before build
Still fills the canvas with the given baseline (~5,000 calls/month) and data owner

expected: Does not name a vendor without a selection criterion

Offers to record the director's decision with its factors and an exit/revisit trigger
